classes.meaning: Changes the bytes-to-tree result of a region. Enters only through SyntaxProfileId inside the existing verter_identity ParseKey (PAR0 G07). The parse tree stays lossless (PAR0 PD05), so presentation choices such as whitespace condensing or comment dropping are never Parse.
Changes the framework meaning computed over admitted parses: bindings, reactivity, macro and prop semantics, component naming and scope identity, CSS-module key surfaces, namespace and mode facts.
Changes which demanded fact families, regions, style stages and product topology (inline versus separate, block participation) the compile structure for one product contains.
Changes how one target lowers the structure: backend selection, dev versus production branches, hoisting and caching plans, whitespace and comment policy, custom-element mode, IDE projection policy.
Changes only the emitted bytes and maps of an already planned target: helper module specifiers, default-export spelling, TypeScript stripping of output, MapMode, version disclosure, style trimming.

Changes only host assembly, decoration, serialization or presentation of an already emitted artifact set: SSR manifest key, HMR decoration, map serialization encoding, output/presentation/serialization profiles.

No Verter stage consumes the option. Admission returns the typed Unsupported outcome on presence, on every route. An option whose impact cannot be classified is Refused until an owning amendment classifies it (CMP0 abort rule).

rules: OI01. Every caller-settable field of CompileRequest, FrameworkCompileRequest, VueCompileRequest, SvelteCompileRequest and the CompileProduct requests has exactly one row and exactly one class.
OI02. A row enters the key of its class and, by chaining, every later key of the same product. It never enters an earlier key.
OI03. A framework row enters keys only of products whose typed framework request is that framework. A Vue row never enters a Svelte product's key, and the reverse.
OI04. MapMode and map demand are Emit; map serialization encoding is Terminal. Neither enters ParseKey, SemanticKey, CompileStructureKey or TargetPlanKey.

OI05. Common execution controls (cancellation, budgets, audit capture, scheduler hints) have no row and enter no key. A control that changes output bytes is an option and must be classified here first.
OI06. A row whose current status is not 'routed' is a defect against CMP-F01/CMP-F02 or a planned refusal; CMP1 routes it to its class or refuses it at the single admission (CMP-D15).

statusValues.routed: read by its stage on every production route that admits it
statusValues.partially-routed: read on some production routes or for some products only
statusValues.unread: admitted on the standalone route and read by no stage; refused on presence by the host integration route
statusValues.refused: refused on presence at request construction on every route
statusValues.host-refused: admitted by construction, refused by the host integration route, and read by the standalone route
statusValues.duplicate-authority: a second spelling of a fact another row already carries

rows.note: Each product roots its own key chain from its own demanded closure; adding a product never changes another product's keys (CN03).

The framework discriminant is FrameworkProfileId (VID0 I05). It is the profile identity in the SemanticKey composition (SK03), never a FrameworkTag spelling (VID0 R03) and never TypeScriptSemanticProfileId. CPF1 lands the value; the slot is already this type.

TypeScriptSemanticProfileId (verter_identity::profile). Enters SemanticKey once, as this Semantic-class option byte, not as a second composition field beside FrameworkProfileId (SK03). Read by the standalone route only; the host bundle refuses it (UnroutableHostRequestAxis::SemanticProfile).
